stem: Which patient is the classic candidate for a CDC Protective Environment room?

options.A: A stable adult with uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia and no major immunocompromising condition.
options.B: A patient after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation who requires protection from environmental fungal exposure.
options.C: Every patient admitted with a large burn regardless of transplant status or infection risk.
options.D: A patient with influenza who needs source-control and transmission-based measures rather than protection from environmental fungi.

rationale: CDC's Protective Environment recommendations are specifically designed for allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipients to reduce exposure to environmental fungi such as Aspergillus. Protective Environment features include HEPA filtration, positive pressure relative to the corridor, a well-sealed room, and appropriate air exchanges. B is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize allogeneic HSCT recipients as the classic CDC population for a Protective Environment intended to reduce environmental fungal exposure.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Appendix A, Table 5 — Components of a Protective Environment
source_locator: Table 5: Patients — allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) only; environmental controls include central/point-of-use HEPA filtration, positive pressure relative to corridor, well-sealed rooms and specified air exchanges.
source_claim_supported: CDC Protective Environment recommendations are specifically intended for allogeneic HSCT patients to reduce exposure to environmental fungal spores.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and environmental safety measures appropriate to client risk.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Protective Environment for allogeneic HSCT

source_original.stem: Which patient is the classic candidate for a CDC Protective Environment room?

options.A: A stable adult with uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia and no major immunocompromising condition
options.B: An allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipient who needs protection from environmental fungi
options.C: Every patient admitted with a large burn regardless of transplant status or specific infection risk
options.D: A patient with seasonal influenza who requires droplet rather than protective-environment precautions

source_original.rationale: CDC Protective Environment recommendations are designed specifically for allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipients to reduce exposure to environmental fungi such as Aspergillus. This room category is not a universal isolation approach for pneumonia, influenza, or all burn patients.
source_original.source_detail: Appendix A, Table 5: Protective Environment — allogeneic HSCT patients; HEPA filtration, positive pressure, well-sealed rooms and related environmental controls.

correction_summary: Retained key B, made the allogeneic-HSCT-only scope explicit, distinguished PE from source-isolation precautions, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC Protective Environment guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: CDC Table 5 page dated 2023-11-27 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Appendix A Table 5, Patients: allogeneic HSCT only
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the CDC-defined PE population and environmental-fungal rationale without extending the indication to other conditions.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because uncomplicated pneumonia does not by itself indicate PE.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because burns are not the CDC PE target population.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because influenza transmission precautions address source transmission rather than the PE goal.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B matches the CDC PE indication.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe patient populations with differing infection-control needs.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — environmental infection prevention.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read CDC Table 5 and isolation guidance, all choices, rationale and NCSBN mapping. B remained uniquely correct.
